item.title: Unheard. Unserved: Black women face added health care barriers as race, gender intersect
item.description: In the final installment of the Global News' series Unheard. Unserved, we look how gender and race can intersect to create even deeper gaps in treatment and outcomes for women.

item.title: Alberta food banks grapple with high cost of free beef
item.description: Rural Alberta food banks are seeking provincial funding to support a program that sees cattle producers donate animals to organizations that feed people in need.

item.title: Greenwashing laws are changing. Businesses are relieved, but environmentalists have concerns
item.description: Laws about greenwashing — making a false or misleading statement about the environmental benefits of a product — will remain on the books, but the Liberal government has said it will be making changes aimed at offering businesses more certainty about what runs afoul of the law.

item.title: Yoplait Yop yogurt drinks recalled in Canada over plastic contamination fears
item.description: Many of Yoplait's yogurts have been pulled from Canadian shelves after the company shared fears over pieces of plastic in some products.

item.title: Reported illnesses have tripled in some school districts. Experts say mental health is a factor
item.description: A CBC investigation finds that school time lost due to reported illness is up in all districts that provided data — more than tripling in some places compared to five years ago. While the data doesn’t say why, experts say deteriorating mental health is causing some kids to stay home.

item.title: Carney says he'll speak with Trump ‘when it's appropriate'
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he doesn't have a "burning issue" to speak with President Donald Trump and would speak with him "when it's appropriate."
